name: Arthur T. Packard
role: Editor of the Bad Lands Cow Boy; Medora stage line manager
bio: Arthur T. Packard was the editor of the Bad Lands Cow Boy, which he launched at Little Missouri, beside Medora, in February 1884 and marked as one year old in January 1885. In his first months he started a museum of Bad Lands curiosities at the office, became the local agent for Studebaker wagons, and fought rival Dickinson over the freight route to Deadwood. In August 1884 he went to St. Paul to close the contracts for the Medora Forwarding and Stage Company, and in September the paper called him the stage line's general manager as he left for Pierre as a delegate to the Republican territorial convention. The Cow Boy office also sold receipts for the Medora coal mine and wrote insurance, and Packard advertised barb wire for sale in 1886. His editorials took on the Custer County ring, a libelous Bismarck telegram about Medora in 1886, and the leaders of the South Dakota statehood movement, and in March 1886 he was named a judge for the Billings County election.
